message.content:
Making poached eggs at home is easier than you might think! Here's a step-by-step guide based on expert techniques:

## What You'll Need
- Fresh eggs (cold)
- White vinegar (or white wine vinegar/apple cider vinegar)
- A large, wide saucepan or pot
- A small bowl or ramekin per egg
- A fine mesh strainer (optional but recommended)
- A slotted spoon
- Paper towels

## Step-by-Step Instructions

### 1. Prepare the Water
Fill a wide saucepan with about 2-3 inches of water and heat over medium-high heat until it reaches a **gentle simmer** — not a rolling boil. You should see small bubbles on the bottom of the pan, but minimal bubbling at the surface. Reduce heat to maintain this temperature.

### 2. Prep the Egg (Optional but Recommended)
For the neatest shape, crack the egg into a **fine mesh strainer** over a sink and gently swirl to drain off the thin, watery part of the white. Then transfer the strained egg to a small bowl or ramekin. This step prevents wispy white strands in the water.

### 3. Add Vinegar
Stir about **1 tablespoon of white vinegar** into the simmering water. The vinegar helps the egg white coagulate and hold its shape. Don't worry — you won't taste it in the finished egg.

### 4. Create a Vortex (for single eggs)
Use a spoon to stir the water in a **circular motion**, creating a whirlpool or vortex in the center. This helps wrap the white around the yolk.

### 5. Cook the Egg
Gently slide the egg from the bowl into the **center of the vortex**. Let it cook undisturbed for **2½ to 3 minutes** for runny yolks, or up to 4 minutes for firmer yolks. The white should be set and opaque.

### 6. Remove and Drain
Use a slotted spoon to lift the poached egg out, letting excess water drip off. Place on a **paper towel-lined plate** briefly to absorb any remaining water.

### 7. Serve
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately on toast, English muffins, avocado toast, or as part of eggs Benedict.

---

## Pro Tips

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|-------------|
| **Use the freshest eggs possible** | Fresh whites hold together better and create less wispy spread |
| **Use cold eggs straight from the fridge** | They hold their shape better when hitting the hot water |
| **Don't overcrowd the pot** | Cook 1-4 eggs at a time; too many lowers the water temperature |
| **Maintain gentle simmer** | Boiling water will break apart the delicate whites |
| **For multiple eggs**, skip the vortex and gently lower them one by one with space between them | The vortex only works well for single eggs |

## Make-Ahead Option
You can poach eggs ahead of time! Immediately transfer cooked eggs to a bowl of **ice water**, then refrigerate in fresh cold water for up to 4-5 days. To reheat, submerge in hot tap water for 20-30 seconds until warmed through.

3. https://www.simplyrecipes.com/recipes/easy_poached_eggs/
4. https://themodernproper.com/poached-eggs
5. https://preppykitchen.com/how-to-poach-an-egg/
